note: This skill encodes an intake/scoping methodology, not jurisdiction-specific legal facts. Claims below are about the method and the authoritative professional-conduct standards it aligns to, plus the local script self-check. No live matter was reviewed and no conflicts search was run. The core discipline is anti-assumption: conflicts are never treated as clear without a real records search, and no fee number goes out without its scope attached.

claims.claim: A lawyer must check for and manage conflicts of interest before acting for a client; a conflicts check requires searching the firm's actual client/adverse-party records, not judging from memory, and a positive conflict blocks opening the file absent informed consent.
claims.raw_snippet: ABA Model Rule 1.7: a lawyer shall not represent a client if the representation involves a concurrent conflict of interest, absent informed written consent where waivable.

claims.claim: Legal fees must be reasonable and the basis of the fee should be communicated to the client, preferably in writing; this underpins attaching scope and assumptions to any fee estimate and distinguishing an estimate from a fixed quote.
claims.raw_snippet: ABA Model Rule 1.5: a lawyer shall not charge an unreasonable fee; the basis or rate of the fee should be communicated to the client, preferably in writing.

claims.claim: Regulatory client-care rules require checking for conflicts and giving the client clear information on costs at the outset of a matter, supporting the intake gate of conflicts-cleared plus scope-and-fee-in-writing before opening.
claims.raw_snippet: SRA Code of Conduct: solicitors must not act where there is an own-interest or client conflict, and must give clients information on costs and how the matter will be handled.

claims.claim: The limitation/prescription (time-bar) date is the highest-stakes item in intake; if unknown or contested it must be resolved first, because a missed limitation date is a classic negligence exposure and an imminent bar can decide whether the firm accepts the matter at all.
claims.raw_snippet: The limitation/prescription date is the highest-stakes row. If unknown or contested -> HIGH, resolve first. Always record the source and the calculation, never a bare date.

claims.claim: The bundled intake_check.py is Python stdlib only (no network, no third-party deps) and ships an embedded self-check runnable via --selftest, which passes; it scores intake completeness and blocks file-opening on pending conflicts or a missing limitation date, and does NOT run the conflicts search or judge the merits.
claims.raw_snippet: `python scripts/intake_check.py --selftest` prints 'selftest OK'. Verified 2026-07-09 on python3.11. Completeness checker only; does not run the conflicts search or judge merits.
